artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of a whole Ambrosian
Missal of 1640, 59,670 LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR bytes, no form
feeds, no NUL bytes, ending in a newline. Registered as a source artifact and
nothing more; deliberately NOT structured as liturgical records. THERE ARE NO
PAGE BOUNDARIES IN THIS FILE.

OCR QUALITY, AND IT IS SERVICEABLE. Measured here by scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a
Latin function-word share of 0.1086 over 238,161 tokens, English 0.0298,
classified `prose-latin`. That is above the ten per cent at which that tool says
running Latin prose sits, and it is the class the 1862 Pustet and the 1924 Braga
fall in. The damage that remains is ordinary for a red-and-black roman-type folio
of this date: long s read as f throughout (`Miffali`, `facrarum`, `Epifc.`),
ligatures and the ae-digraph unstable, and -- more consequentially -- THE BOOK
SETS TWO COLUMNS TO THE PAGE AND THE SCAN INTERLEAVES THEM, so consecutive lines
frequently belong to different columns and a sentence read straight down the file
is often two sentences shuffled. Read a locus, do not read a run.

A HEADING SPLIT ACROSS A COLUMN BREAK IS INVISIBLE TO A LINE-BY-LINE SEARCH, AND
THAT IS A METHOD WARNING THIS LANE LEARNED THE HARD WAY. The first anachronism
sweep of this acquisition was run line by line over the text layers and missed
two post-imprint saints in the sister 1712 volume, because their headings were
broken across two lines by the column interleave. The sweep was rebuilt to probe
whole leaves through the item's per-leaf recognition and the missing saints
appeared at once. Any later negative search over this file must do the same, or
say that it did not.

ST CHARLES BORROMEO IS IN THIS FILE AND THE PROBE THAT LOOKED FOR HIM MISSED HIM.
The index at leaf n7 has `Caroli, Epifc.Mcdiol.4.Nouembris. 55o` and the body has
`S. Caroli,Epi(c. Mediol. folemne.` at line 3376. The automated probe searched for
`Borromaei` and for `Caroli ... Mediol`, and failed on both counts: this book
never uses the surname, and the scan reads `Mediol` as `Mcdiol`. He was found by
reading. He is 1610 and therefore expected in a 1640 book, so nothing turns on
him -- but a battery that can miss a saint it is hunting is a battery whose
negatives carry that limit, and it is recorded on the artifact rather than only
in the rights file.

WHAT THE FILE CONTAINS AND WHERE, READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Cardinal Cesare
Monti's letter to the clergy of Milan opens the book at leaf n6, line 7. The
alphabetical index of saints celebrated in the Missal runs at n7 to n8. The
kalendar runs month by month from n9 (January) to n20. The `TABELLA TEMPORARIA
FESTORVM MOBILIVM` and its rubrics are at n22 to n24. The rubrics of the Mass and
the ceremonial follow from about n27. The temporal, sanctoral and Commons occupy
the body. The book closes with Holy Saturday and the Vigil of Pentecost, the
Blessing of Water and the Aspersion, ending `F I N I S.` at n767.

IDENTITY AND EXTENT. Internet Archive item `bub_gb_6ApfhlfCMksC`, 772 leaves,
`imagecount = 772`, matching the 772 `<OBJECT>` elements of the item's own
djvu.xml counted here. Google id 6ApfhlfCMksC, OCLC 954958440, contributor
National Central Library of Rome, uploaded 2014-11-12 by
`tools.bub@tools.wmflabs.org`. The catalogue collation is `[36], 554, 176 p.` in
folio with the note `Testo stampato in rosso e nero`, and the frontispiece and
illustrations are engraved by Cesare Bassano. The companion page-image container
is the item's `bub_gb_6ApfhlfCMksC.pdf`, 78,039,485 bytes, which is not
registered: this repository has no cause to hold 78 MB of images it can re-fetch,
and the two readings taken from the images here -- the engraved title page -- were
taken from the item's per-leaf derivative.

WHAT A READER MUST DO BEFORE READING ANY LITURGY OUT OF THIS BOOK. `read_from =
"not-read"` on the witness row in
src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml is still correct and was not
touched by the lane that wrote this record. Nothing in this repository has read a
unit of the Ambrosian use.
artifacts.rights_basis:
Public domain in the United States because the book was first published outside
the United States before the pre-1931 line, and on that ground alone.

THE LINE, AND THE YEAR IT WAS DERIVED FOR. Any work first published abroad before
1931 is out of United States copyright; that is the line guidance/missals.md
records from Cornell's public-domain chart as current on 1 January 2026. THE LINE
MOVES EVERY JANUARY -- guidance/missals.md:249 states it in terms -- so it is
written here as DERIVED FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2026 and not as a standing rule: on
1 January 2027 it becomes before 1932, and a later reader must re-derive it
rather than quote this sentence. Publication in 1640 clears the 2026 line by two
hundred and ninety-one years and every later line by more. URAA restoration
cannot reach it: a restored term runs at most 95 years from publication, which
for 1640 ended in 1735.

THE DATE WAS TESTED AGAINST THE BOOK'S OWN PAGES, TWICE AND INDEPENDENTLY. The
engraved title page at leaf n4 of 772 is lettered `MEDIOLANI / Apud Io. Ambrosium
Sirturu, haer. Pontij, & Picaleae, Impress. Archiep. M DC XL`, read in the page
image because the engraving carries no machine-readable text. Independently, the
book's own paschal table opens at 1640 and its rubric calls 1640 `nunc
currentis`, the current year. A thirty-two-probe anachronism battery over all 772
leaves found nothing later than the imprint; the probes and their negatives are
listed in src/sources/inventories/ambrosian-and-mozarabic-rights-v1.toml. The
volume ends at `F I N I S.` on leaf n767 with no supplement, no second title page
and no second imprint. See the edition record for the thirty-nine post-1640 years
that stand in the file and are all cells of that paschal table.

THE SCAN AND ITS TEXT LAYER ADD NOTHING FOR ANYONE TO OWN. A faithful mechanical
reproduction of a public-domain work is not original authorship (Bridgeman Art
Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)), and machine optical
character recognition adds no human authorship on top of it: this text layer was
produced autonomously by ABBYY FineReader 9.0, per the item's own `ocr` field,
converted by `abbyy-to-hocr 1.1.11`, and there is no author to hold a right in
it. Bridgeman's limit applies as stated on the Braga record -- it frees a scan of
public-domain matter and says nothing about a scan of anything else -- and there
is nothing else here, because every leaf of this file is a photograph of a page
printed in 1640.

THE GOOGLE QUESTION, WHICH IS REAL AND IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN IGNORED. The book
was scanned by Google for the National Central Library of Rome and the file
carries Google's watermark as OCR noise at line 1, `gitized by Godgle`. IT DOES
NOT CARRY GOOGLE'S `Usage guidelines` PAGE. That page -- modern prose of Google's
own authorship, asking that the files be used for personal, non-commercial
purposes -- IS present in the two Mozarabic artifacts of this lane, and the
position on it is stated once, in the rights record, and applies wherever it
appears. Here the only Google matter is a watermark, which is an image of a word
and not a work. Google's own statement about books like this one is that `Public
domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians`; it asserts
no copyright in the scan and could not sustain one in a faithful reproduction.

NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the
download succeeded, or that the item carries `licenseurl =
http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/`. guidance/sources.md:395-400
holds the first two insufficient for `tracked`, and the third is a fact about an
item's metadata rather than about a book -- the ground refused at
src/sources/inventories/lt-hist-rights-audit-v1.toml. This basis would be
unchanged if the item carried no mark or a contradictory one.

edition.authority: Cesare Monti, Cardinal Priest of S. Maria Transpontina and Archbishop of Milan, by his own letter to the whole clergy of Milan printed at the head of the book. NOT a papal instrument and not a decree of a Roman congregation: this is a metropolitan legislating for his own use, which is the ordinary constitutional shape of the Latin diocesan uses and the shape Braga's 1924 is the exception to.
edition.publication: Missale Ambrosianum. Mediolani, Apud Io. Ambrosium Sirturum, haer. Pontij, & Picaleae, Impress. Archiep., M DC XL. Engraved title page signed C. Bassanus F. (Cesare Bassano). The copy digitised is the National Central Library of Rome's, scanned by Google and uploaded to the Internet Archive as item bub_gb_6ApfhlfCMksC. The catalogue collation is [36], 554, 176 p., folio, text printed in red and black.
edition.title: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan: Io. Ambrosius Sirturus and the heirs of Ponzio and Piccaglia, 1640

alternate_titles: Missale iuxta ritum sanctae ecclesiae Mediolanensis
work.author: Archdiocese of Milan
work.description: The altar book of the Ambrosian rite -- the Latin use of the church of Milan, the largest non-Roman Latin rite still celebrated, and one of the uses left standing by the exempting clause of Quo primum. It is a Missal in the ordinary sense and it is NOT the Missale Romanum: it carries its own kalendar with its own Milanese archbishop-saints, its own Ordo Missae and Canon, a temporal cycle that begins six Sundays before Christmas, its own Holy Week and Easter Vigil, Commons, votive and Requiem Masses, blessings and Mass tones. IT MUST NOT BE FILED WITH THE ROMAN BOOK. work.catholic-church.missale-romanum is the Roman Rite's book; this is a different rite's, and the edge that does not exist between them is the point -- src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml records at its own line note that drawing one from the Roman line into the Ambrosian would assert a derivation in exactly the direction history runs the other way. It is registered under the archdiocese, on the pattern of work.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense, because the rite is the church of Milan's and the authority over the book has been the archbishop's throughout its printed tradition. The three editions registered here are printings, not promulgations: none of them carries a papal instrument, and what the 1640 and 1712 carry instead is an archbishop's own letter to his clergy.
work.title: Missale Ambrosianum
